newsitem.title: USA: Church deacon sentenced in L.A. exorcism case.
newsitem.headline: Church deacon sentenced in L.A. exorcism case.

text.p: A church deacon was sentenced to three years probation on Wednesday and ordered to perform community service for his role in a violent exorcism ritual that led to the death of a female Korean missionary.

Jin Hyn Choi, 47, a deacon with the Calvary Presbyterian Church in suburban Glendale, had earlier pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter in the July 1996 death of 53-year-old Kyung Jae Chung, who died of crushed internal organs in the exorcism, which lasted several hours.

Choi testified for the prosecution in the trial of Chung's husband Jae Whoa Chung, 44, and Sung Soo Choi, 42, an underground missionary in China who led the exorcism ritual, known as "ansu kido," and who is not related to the church deacon.
Judge James Albracht found the two guilty of involuntary manslaughter following a three-week, non-jury trial and last week sentenced Chung to two years in prison and Sung Soo Choi to four years.

In sentencing Jin Hyn Choi to probation on Wednesday, Albracht noted that while he had taken part in the exorcism, he had played a minor role and said the woman's death was "a tragic case for all involved."
During his testimony, Jin Hyn Choi testified that he and the other two men took turns "stomping" on the victim's chest to rid her of demons until they noticed that her chest had "dipped."
An autopsy report said Kyung Jae Chung suffered "excruciatingly painful" injuries and looked as if she had been "run over by a car."
The Chungs, who ran a Christian school in Bangladesh, and Sung Soo Choi, were in Los Angeles for prayer meeting when the exorcism, to which the victim had agreed, took place.
